main_body: Dark stone throne seen straight from the front: tall pointed backrest with gold trim, red cushion seat, arms on both sides and a stepped plinth base
top_band: none: the middle column goes from the dark backrest (rows 4-17) straight into the red cushion at rows 18-23, which is a vertical face with a cream/gold lower edge. There is no lighter horizontal surface seen from above.
evidence: The throne is drawn as a straight front elevation. The red cushion (rows 18-23) is a graded face-on band from light pink to red, not a seat top. The seat has no lighter horizontal band above a front face, and the arm caps are only 1-2px gold lines (rows 17-18). The backrest, arms and plinth are all flat vertical faces. The seat surface cannot be seen from above, so it fails the seat requirement.

style.evidence: The body is made of a few near-black and dark grey tones with gold trim and a graded red cushion. Large areas of the backrest and base are flat dark fills with no stone grain, cracks or per-block shading. The outline is neutral near-black, which reads as a sticker, whereas the Beodeul references use tinted dark material tones and carry much more texture per tile. The red cushion gradient and gold trim are the only richer parts.
